investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-26T21:40–21:48Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), causing every remote agent pod to remain Unschedulable and preventing any VM from being assigned. Because no VM was ever scheduled, the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, so all four required evidence fields are missing and both contract assertions (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState oneOf running/idle/ready) are unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the two nodes that carry that label. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector at all. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") never progresses past pod scheduling, so no VM ID or remote state is ever returned, and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259) is fully violated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — confirms full cluster scheduling exhaustion for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=130123, status=fail — pod was stuck unscheduled for 125s before the check timed out, well before the 240000ms warning threshold, indicating an immediate hard block rather than a slow response.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent — the runner never reached the point of creating or inspecting a VM.

expected-output.contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 256–259): assertions vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] are both unmet because no VM was ever provisioned.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduling error message, latencyMs=151782, endedAt=2026-06-26T21:45:37Z — confirms the capacity exhaustion persisted across sequential eval runs.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduling error message, latencyMs=152285, endedAt=2026-06-26T21:48:09Z — confirms exhaustion was still present ~7 minutes after the first failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885 (line 1885): createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) — the runner explicitly requests a remote (kata peer-pod) machine type, which requires the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187 (line 183): remote-agent-create is marked required=true with degradedAfterFailures=1, meaning this single failure is sufficient to mark the feature degraded.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the two eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing pods and no preemption victims exist, leaving zero capacity for new remote agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or label drift on 4 of 6 nodes: those nodes may have lost the required label (e.g., kata.peerpods.io/vm or an equivalent node selector label) due to a node pool update, node replacement, or label mutation, reducing the schedulable pool from 6 to 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity shortage.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote agent pods from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if cleanup (withCleanup in the runner) failed on a previous run, orphaned pods could be occupying the limited VM slots.

Lower confidence — cluster autoscaler not configured or unable to provision new kata-capable nodes in time: if the node pool does not autoscale for kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes, a burst of concurrent remote agent requests would exhaust capacity with no recovery path.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl shows that kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is non-zero on the eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the root cause would not be resource exhaustion and another explanation (e.g., a quota policy, admission webhook rejection, or API-level error) would need to be investigated.

Add a cleanup-verification eval step that confirms no orphaned remote agent pods remain after each eval run, catching leaked pods that would silently consume VM slots across runs.

Consider a pre-flight scheduling check within the remote-agent-create eval that queries node capacity before attempting pod creation, enabling faster and more specific failure messages when capacity is known to be zero.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment between 21:43 and 21:48 UTC on 2026-06-26 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returned an agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across the two eligible nodes at the time of the eval run. The remaining 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, the agent pod remained Unschedulable for 145 seconds before the eval timed out. This prevented createAgent from completing, so the runner never reached the state-polling logic and produced no evidence, causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to report all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) as missing. This is an eval infrastructure failure reflecting a real resource constraint in the production Kubernetes cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: the cluster had no remaining VM slots for peer-pod scheduling at the time of the eval run, and preemption found no victims to evict. All three sibling checks report the same error, confirming this is a shared infrastructure constraint rather than a per-check logic bug.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod requires a specific node label or taint (e.g., a kata/peer-pods capable node pool) that only 2 nodes satisfy. If those 2 nodes are also at VM capacity, the effective schedulable pool is zero. A misconfigured or missing node label on additional nodes would reduce the eligible pool further.

Tertiary — concurrent workload contention: other pods or eval runs may have consumed the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on the 2 eligible nodes just before this eval run, leaving no capacity. This would be a transient condition rather than a persistent misconfiguration.

Lower probability — eval runner token or org resolution failure causing createAgent to be called with invalid arguments: the runner does check for a missing token at line 1902 and would return SKIP rather than fail, so this path is unlikely given the scheduling error message is explicit.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-26T21:40–21:48Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), causing every remote agent pod to remain Unschedulable and preventing any VM from being assigned. Because no VM was ever scheduled, the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, so all four required evidence fields are missing and both contract assertions (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState oneOf running/idle/ready) are unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the two nodes that carry that label. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector at all. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") never progresses past pod scheduling, so no VM ID or remote state is ever returned, and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259) is fully violated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — confirms full cluster scheduling exhaustion for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=130123, status=fail — pod was stuck unscheduled for 125s before the check timed out, well before the 240000ms warning threshold, indicating an immediate hard block rather than a slow response.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent — the runner never reached the point of creating or inspecting a VM.

expected-output.contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 256–259): assertions vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] are both unmet because no VM was ever provisioned.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduling error message, latencyMs=151782, endedAt=2026-06-26T21:45:37Z — confirms the capacity exhaustion persisted across sequential eval runs.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduling error message, latencyMs=152285, endedAt=2026-06-26T21:48:09Z — confirms exhaustion was still present ~7 minutes after the first failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885 (line 1885): createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) — the runner explicitly requests a remote (kata peer-pod) machine type, which requires the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187 (line 183): remote-agent-create is marked required=true with degradedAfterFailures=1, meaning this single failure is sufficient to mark the feature degraded.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the two eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing pods and no preemption victims exist, leaving zero capacity for new remote agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or label drift on 4 of 6 nodes: those nodes may have lost the required label (e.g., kata.peerpods.io/vm or an equivalent node selector label) due to a node pool update, node replacement, or label mutation, reducing the schedulable pool from 6 to 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity shortage.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote agent pods from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if cleanup (withCleanup in the runner) failed on a previous run, orphaned pods could be occupying the limited VM slots.

Lower confidence — cluster autoscaler not configured or unable to provision new kata-capable nodes in time: if the node pool does not autoscale for kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes, a burst of concurrent remote agent requests would exhaust capacity with no recovery path.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment between 21:43 and 21:48 UTC on 2026-06-26 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returned an agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across the two eligible nodes at the time of the eval run. The remaining 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, the agent pod remained Unschedulable for 145 seconds before the eval timed out. This prevented createAgent from completing, so the runner never reached the state-polling logic and produced no evidence, causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to report all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) as missing. This is an eval infrastructure failure reflecting a real resource constraint in the production Kubernetes cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

All three sibling checks report the same error, confirming this is a shared infrastructure constraint rather than a per-check logic bug.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod requires a specific node label or taint (e.g., a kata/peer-pods capable node pool) that only 2 nodes satisfy. If those 2 nodes are also at VM capacity, the effective schedulable pool is zero. A misconfigured or missing node label on additional nodes would reduce the eligible pool further.

Lower probability — eval runner token or org resolution failure causing createAgent to be called with invalid arguments: the runner does check for a missing token at line 1902 and would return SKIP rather than fail, so this path is unlikely given the scheduling error message is explicit.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes nodes show available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the failure, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and an alternative cause (e.g., API-level rejection, auth failure, or runner bug) would need to be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., concurrent workload contention) rather than a persistent capacity or configuration problem.
If only remote-agent-state fails while remote-agent-create passes in a subsequent run, the root cause would be localized to the state-polling logic rather than shared pod scheduling infrastructure.

If the pod scheduling error message changes to a different error (e.g., image pull failure, auth error, or quota exceeded on a different resource), the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion diagnosis would not apply.
If node affinity/selector rules are confirmed to match more than 2 nodes, the 4-node exclusion hypothesis would be disproved and a different node configuration issue would need to be identified.

Add a VM cleanup verification eval that confirms peer-pod VMs allocated by prior eval runs are fully released after withCleanup completes, to detect VM slot leaks that could cause progressive quota exhaustion.

Add a node affinity/selector health eval that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote agent pod's scheduling requirements, alerting if the eligible node count drops below a configured minimum.
Add a historical trend eval that tracks kata.peerpods.io/vm usage over time across eval runs to detect gradual quota exhaustion before it causes scheduling failures.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-26 because newly requested pods could not be scheduled: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence was collected by any check, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned and the runtime response contract could not be satisfied.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had insufficient remaining capacity, and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never completed, no evidence was returned, and all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this eval run.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for a new remote agent pod.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's required node affinity or selector labels, narrowing the schedulable pool to only the 2 kata-capable nodes that are already full.
Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the cluster is insufficient to absorb concurrent eval probe runs alongside production workloads.
Lower probability — transient resource spike: a burst of concurrent remote agent requests temporarily exhausted VM slots; capacity may have recovered after the eval window closed.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the 2 kata-capable nodes show available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the eval run, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint must be investigated.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and the pod schedules normally, the failure was a transient capacity spike rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.
If the pod spec's node affinity or selector was recently changed to exclude nodes that previously matched, the root cause would shift to a configuration change rather than capacity exhaustion.
If the 4 non-kata nodes were intentionally excluded by design and the 2 kata nodes had capacity, the failure would point to a quota or limit-range constraint rather than raw resource exhaustion.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is defined on any node in the cluster, the cause would be a missing node resource registration rather than exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on all eligible nodes and warns when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold, providing earlier signal before pod scheduling fails.

Add an eval that verifies the remote agent pod's node affinity and selector rules match at least a minimum number of Ready nodes in the cluster, catching label drift before it narrows the schedulable pool to zero.

Add a scheduling-latency eval that measures time-to-Running for a remote agent pod and warns when it exceeds a threshold well below the current 144s unschedulable timeout, enabling earlier detection of capacity pressure.

Consider a sibling-correlation eval rule: when all checks under a feature share the same Unschedulable error class, auto-escalate to a shared-dependency investigation rather than treating each check independently.
